rules.title: Rent Stabilization Ordinance - Coverage
rules.requirement: Rent for residential units first built on or before October 1, 1978 is subject to the Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance, including apartments, condominiums (if tenancy commenced before January 1, 1996), townhomes (if tenancy commenced before January 1, 1996), duplexes, multiple single-family units on one parcel, rooms in hotels/motels occupied by the same tenant over 30 days, residential units attached to commercial buildings, ADUs, JADUs, and mobile homes in mobile home parks.
rules.quotedSpan: the RSO applies to rental properties that were first built on or before October 1, 1978, as well as replacement units under LAMC Section 151.28 and if any of the following: Apartment, Condominium (Rent amount is not regulated for tenancies that commenced after December 31, 1995)
rules.coverageDescription: Residential buildings with first certificate of occupancy on or before October 1, 1978; does not apply to condominiums and townhomes with tenancies commenced after December 31, 1995.
exemptions: Condominium or townhome tenancies that commenced after December 31, 1995
warnings: Luxury exemption provision mentioned but details incomplete in source

rules.title: Allowable Annual Rent Increase - General
rules.requirement: Rent under the RSO may be increased once every 12 months by the allowable rent increase percentage set by the city. The landlord can no longer include an additional percentage increase for utilities.
rules.quotedSpan: Rent may be increased once every 12 months by the allowable rent increase percentage (click here to view the allowable rent increase PDF). Effective February 2, 2026, the landlord can no longer include an additional percentage increase for utilities.
rules.coverageDescription: RSO-covered residential rental units built on or before October 1, 1978.
warnings: Specific percentage/formula for allowable increase is referenced but not provided in this source

rules.title: Rent Increase Prohibition - COVID-19 Relief
rules.requirement: Rent increases are prohibited for rental units subject to the RSO.
rules.quotedSpan: Effective March 30, 2020, through January 31, 2024, rent increases are prohibited for rental units subject to the Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO).
rules.coverageDescription: RSO-covered residential rental units built on or before October 1, 1978.
warnings: This period has ended as of the source date; rule is historical

rules.title: Additional Tenant Rent Increase
rules.requirement: A 10% rent increase is allowed if an additional tenant (not a dependent) moves into the rental unit, with notice required within 60 days of learning about the additional tenant. The prior 10% increase for additional dependents is no longer permitted.
rules.quotedSpan: Effective February 2, 2026, an additonal 10% increase for an additional dependent added to the tenancy is no longer permitted. However, a 10% for an additional tenant is allowed (not a dependent) if moves into a rental unit: Landlords can increase the rent within 60 days of learning about the additional tenant.
rules.coverageDescription: RSO-covered residential rental units built on or before October 1, 1978.

rules.title: Registration Fee Surcharge - Monthly
rules.requirement: A landlord may collect 50% of the annual registration fee from the tenant as a monthly surcharge ($38.75 per month as of the effective date), with 30-day notice required.
rules.quotedSpan: Effective January 1, 2020, the surcharge is $38.75. The landlord may pass through 50% of the fee to the tenant every month rather than once a year. A 30-day notice must be given to the tenant to collect a rental surcharge of $1.61.
rules.coverageDescription: RSO-covered residential rental units built on or before October 1, 1978.
warnings: Source contains conflicting amounts ($1.61 vs $38.75); interpretation is that $38.75 is the current effective amount

rules.title: Systematic Code Enforcement Fee Pass-Through
rules.requirement: A landlord may collect 1/12 of 50% of the annual Systematic Code Enforcement Fee from the tenant each month.
rules.quotedSpan: Effective January 1, 2022, a landlord may collect 1/12 of 50% of the annual Systematic Code Enforcement Fee from the tenant of the rental unit per month. (Added by Ord. No. 187,108, Eff. 8/6/21.)
rules.coverageDescription: RSO-covered residential rental units built on or before October 1, 1978.

rules.title: Smoke Detector/Carbon Monoxide Detector Surcharge
rules.requirement: A landlord may add a $3.00 monthly surcharge to rent for the installation and cost of a hard-wired smoke detector or combination smoke/carbon monoxide detector.
rules.quotedSpan: A $3.00 surcharge may be added to the rent for the installation and cost of a hard-wired smoke detector or a combination smoke/carbon monoxide detector.
rules.coverageDescription: RSO-covered residential rental units built on or before October 1, 1978.

rules.title: Just Cause Eviction - Tenant At-Fault Reasons
rules.requirement: A landlord may evict a tenant for the following at-fault reasons: failure to pay rent, failure to fix or address a violation of the rental agreement, creating a nuisance or causing damage to the rental unit, using the rental unit for an illegal purpose, failure to renew a similar rental agreement, failure to provide reasonable access to the rental unit, or if the person at lease end is a subtenant not approved by the landlord.
rules.quotedSpan: Tenant is at-fault: Failure to pay rent; Failure to fix or address a violation of the rental agreement; Creating a nuisance or causing damage to the rental unit; Using the rental unit for an illegal purpose; Failure to renew a similar rental agreement; Failure to provide the landlord with reasonable access to the rental unit; The person at the end of the lease term is a subtenant not approved by the landlord
rules.coverageDescription: RSO-covered residential rental units built on or before October 1, 1978.

rules.title: Just Cause Eviction - Tenant Not-At-Fault Reasons
rules.requirement: A landlord may evict a tenant for no-fault reasons: the owner or immediate family member will move into the rental unit, a resident manager will move into the rental unit, demolition and permanent removal from the rental market, government order, or conversion to affordable housing.
rules.quotedSpan: Tenant is not at-fault: The owner or immediate family member will move into the rental unit; A resident manager will move into the rental unit; Demolition and permanent removal from the rental market; Government order; Conversion to affordable housing
rules.coverageDescription: RSO-covered residential rental units built on or before October 1, 1978.

rules.title: Eviction Notice Filing Requirement
rules.requirement: All notices to terminate a tenancy for RSO rental units must be filed with the Los Angeles Housing Department within three business days of service on the tenant.
rules.quotedSpan: All notices to terminate a tenancy for all rental units subject to City's Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) must be filed with the Los Angeles Housing Department (LAHD) within three (3) business days of service on the tenant per Los Angeles Municipal Code 151.09.C.9 & 165.05.B.5.
rules.coverageDescription: RSO-covered residential rental units built on or before October 1, 1978.

rules.title: No-Fault Eviction Tenant Relocation Assistance
rules.requirement: Landlords must pay tenant relocation assistance for no-fault evictions (owner move-in, resident manager move-in, demolition, government order, or conversion to affordable housing). A 30-day and 60-day written notice is required (some evictions require 120-day notice or up to a 1-year extension).
rules.quotedSpan: No-fault evictions require the payment of relocation assistance. Give the tenant a 30-day and 60-day written notice (some evictions require 120-day notice or up to a 1-year extension). Payment of tenant relocation assistance.
rules.coverageDescription: RSO-covered residential rental units built on or before October 1, 1978.
warnings: Specific relocation assistance amounts not provided in source; notice periods partially unclear

rules.title: Right to Counsel Notice Requirement
rules.requirement: Landlords must post and provide tenants with a Notice of Right to Counsel at the start of the tenancy, and also attach it to any eviction notice or termination of rental subsidy notice.
rules.quotedSpan: Beginning August 20, 2025, landlords must post the Notice of Right to Counsel and provide it to the tenant at the start of the tenancy. The Notice must also be attached to a copy of any eviction notice or termination of a rental subsidy.
rules.coverageDescription: RSO-covered residential rental units built on or before October 1, 1978.

rules.title: Interest Payments on Security Deposits
rules.requirement: The RSO requires interest payments on security deposits, with specific rules set by the Rent Adjustment Commission.
rules.coverageDescription: RSO-covered residential rental units built on or before October 1, 1978.
warnings: Source provides no details on interest rate, calculation method, or payment timeline
